clue.text: Peculiarity, having no name attached to grand idol

parts.note: G is a common abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: having no name means the abbreviation for name is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: peculiarity is oddness, strangeness

explanation.surface: Someone's odd quirk, published anonymously, gets linked to a great object of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes N from ODDNESS to leave ODDESS, which is 'attached to' G.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol can be a worshipped deity, and a female deity is exactly this.

clue.text: In Georgia, dread such aggressive music

indicators.note: In Georgia places the word for dread inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
angst is a feeling of dread or anxiety

explanation.surface: Someone in Georgia fears this kind of hostile music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' only links wordplay to definition; 'In' is the container signal, not part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangsta rap is a hip-hop style known for its violent, confrontational lyrics.

clue.text: Shamed by defeat over Times leader

parts.note: to dish an opponent is to defeat or ruin them
on means over, concerning, as in a row over money
the Times setter speaks of the paper as ours, so its leader, the editor, is our ed

explanation.surface: Someone humiliated by a defeat concerning the newspaper's editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' is not T: in a Times clue it is OUR ED, our editor, since the paper speaks of itself as ours.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disgraced or brought into public shame is to have lost one's honour.

clue.text: Limbs (not head) — they glow

indicators.note: not head says the first letter of the word for limbs is dropped

parts.note: members are limbs of the body

explanation.surface: A puzzle of body parts without their head that somehow glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not head' takes the M off MEMBERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Embers are small pieces of burning coal or wood still glowing after a fire dies down.

clue.text: Long-distance traveller accepts flying must include relevant service

indicators.note: must include means the service's letters are placed inside the rearranged word
flying suggests letters sent scattering, so the word accepts is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force, is the service relevant to flying

explanation.surface: A traveller covering great distances agrees that flying must involve the air force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' signals the anagram and 'must include' the insertion; the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force, the service relevant to flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle built to travel through outer space covers enormous distances.

clue.text: Day off? Graduates turn to wash

indicators.note: turn says the letters of the word for graduates are read backwards

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates
a bath is a wash

explanation.surface: Students who have graduated take a day off and turn to washing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses BAS into SAB.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekly day of rest kept free of work in religious tradition, hence a day off.

clue.text: You must leave a cube smooth

indicators.note: must leave means the old word for you is taken out of the number

parts.note: a thousand is ten cubed, a cube number
thou is the old word for you

explanation.surface: An instruction to quit a cube and keep things smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must leave' takes THOU out of THOUSAND, ten cubed. 'a cube' looks like an object, but it is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth wood is to rub it down with sandpaper, a verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: Broadcaster announced it will keep buzzers going

parts.note: the Beeb is the nickname of the BBC
read out, as a newsreader announces the news

explanation.surface: A broadcaster announces something that keeps the buzzers working.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beeb is the BBC's British nickname; 'buzzers' are bees, not electrical gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Bee bread is pollen stored by bees as food for the hive, sustaining the insects.

clue.text: Fool is half in agreement

indicators.note: half in picks the front half of the word for agreement

parts.note: assent is agreement

explanation.surface: A fool is only half in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot or dolt is called by this donkey's name.

clue.text: Keep talking about old weapon

indicators.note: about says the phrase goes around the abbreviation for old

parts.note: to harp on is to keep talking about something tediously

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going on about an old weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal here, not 'concerning' as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed spear thrown or fired at whales and large fish.

clue.text: Refusals to shorten feature

indicators.note: to shorten means the last letter of the word for feature is cut off

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Refusals to cut a newspaper feature down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shorten' cuts E from NOSE. 'feature' looks like an article, but it is a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the word for a negative reply, each a refusal.

clue.text: Water fills empty butt, as always getting round problem

indicators.note: fills means the water goes inside the emptied butt
empty leaves only the outside letters of butt

parts.note: rain is water

indicators.note: getting round means the word for always encloses the word as

parts.note: e'er is the poetic short form of ever, always

explanation.surface: Rain fills an empty water butt, as it always does, which is a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outer letters of butt and 'fills' inserts the water; 'getting round' wraps the poetic form of ever round 'as'. A water butt is a garden rain barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or riddle that taxes the mind is a problem to solve.

clue.text: Given cat's instinct, tucking into small fish

definitions.note: read as given the cat is: to be given the cat is to be flogged with a cat-o'-nine-tails, the 's standing for is

indicators.note: tucking into says the instinct goes inside the small fish

parts.note: the cod is a fish
an urge is an instinct

explanation.surface: A cat's natural impulse to tuck into a little fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat's' is cat is: 'Given cat' is the definition, the cat being the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip. 'tucking into' puts URGE into S COD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given the cat meant a flogging, so it equals being whipped.

clue.text: A noble fear is torn clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the words fear is torn wrap around the answer

explanation.surface: A nobleman fears his clothes are torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here: fear is torn clothes (covers) the answer, in feAR IS TOrn.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal word for an aristocrat, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: One entrancing period of work on farm machinery

parts.note: a spell is a stint or period of work
a binder is a reaping machine that binds sheaves

explanation.surface: Someone working a stint on farm machinery holds people enthralled.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesmerising speaker or performer who holds an audience entranced.

clue.text: A danger in horse being accompanied by pointer

indicators.note: in places the danger inside the word for horse

parts.note: a steed is a horse
risk is danger

explanation.surface: A dangerous horse goes along with a pointer dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointer' suggests the dog, but it is the star symbol that points to a footnote.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with the star symbol that points the reader to a note.

clue.text: Where surgeon working, above all?

parts.note: at gives where something is, a location
an op, an operation, is where a surgeon is working

explanation.surface: Where is a surgeon working, above all else?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where surgeon working' reads as AT OP, at an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying on top of everything else is being higher than all of it.

clue.text: Tuna scarce? Switch to crab, perhaps

indicators.note: switch tells the solver to change round the letters of tuna scarce

explanation.surface: With tuna scarce, an angler switches to crab instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' rearranges TUNA SCARCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs are an example of shelled arthropods in this aquatic group, as are lobsters.

clue.text: Its winner most strongly backed

parts.note: in a contest of pulling on a rope, the winners are the team that leans and pulls backwards hardest, not the favourite of the betting

explanation.walkthrough: 'most strongly backed' sounds like betting on a favourite, but the winning team literally pulls back hardest on the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope-pulling contest between two teams is won by the side that hauls backwards most powerfully.

clue.text: Endless fun in tent: magician's beginning to bend small hat

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the big-top show is dropped

parts.note: a circus is fun under a big tent

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of magician's

parts.note: to flex is to bend

explanation.surface: A magician's entertainment in a tent has him bending a small hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts S from CIRCUS; 'beginning' gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: The accent mark shaped like a tiny pointed roof or hat over a letter, as in rôle.

clue.text: Wide boy has change of heart, becoming poet

indicators.note: has change of heart means the central letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: a wide boy is a British term for a shady dealer, a chancer

explanation.surface: A spiv reforms and becomes a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a small-time crook. 'has change of heart' swaps the middle N of CHANCER for U.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey, author of The Canterbury Tales, is England's great medieval poet.

clue.text: Gratified these rags become stylish clothes

definitions.meaning: the word before rags makes a phrase for one's best party clothes

explanation.surface: Pleased that old rags have turned into fashionable clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Glad rags are informal for one's best clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling pleased or gratified is the plain meaning; added before rags it names party finery.

clue.text: Darken joy?

definitions.meaning: to remove light, making something darker

explanation.walkthrough: Split as DE-LIGHT, the word means take the light away.
explanation.definitionFit: Great pleasure is joy; split with the prefix de-, it means to take away light.

clue.text: Took huge interest in American university ball

parts.note: a red is a ball in snooker

explanation.surface: An American university's ball game drew enormous interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huge interest' is not enthusiasm: it is extortionate interest on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Usury is lending money at exorbitant interest, so to usure is to charge it.

clue.text: An Arabian vessel? Yes indeed

parts.note: a dhow is a traditional Arab sailing boat

explanation.surface: Asked whether it is an Arabian boat, someone replies emphatically yes.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic exclamation of agreement, the same as saying yes indeed.

clue.text: Who is going to eat these kitchen scraps?

definitions.text: Who is going to eat these
definitions.meaning: a question answered by naming the farm animals that will
leftover food fed to farm animals

explanation.walkthrough: The question 'Who is going to eat these?' is answered by the answer split in two: farm animals will.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste food from the kitchen fed to farm animals is called by this name.

clue.text: Be sorry to have split from girl

definitions.text: Be sorry to have split from
definitions.meaning: to feel the absence of someone after parting
a young woman, as a title

explanation.definitionFit: To feel someone's absence after a parting is one sense; it is also a title for an unmarried young woman.

clue.text: Receiving wire "Rash wickets lost"

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters of rash wickets are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A headline: rash batting led to wickets being lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges RASH WICKETS.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine wire in an early crystal radio set that touched the crystal to pick up the signal.

clue.text: Arose, it appears, showing a measure of warmth?

indicators.note: it appears refers to how the word appears in the grid: written upwards in a down light, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: arose means got up; the up is supplied by reading the word upwards in this down light

explanation.surface: Something rose up and showed how warm it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it appears' points to the grid: in a down entry, GOT written upwards is GOT up, which means arose.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit for the thermal insulation of duvets and clothing, rating how warm they keep you.

clue.text: Falling over, soldier died — make his grave?

indicators.note: falling over says the letters are turned round

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier fell and died; someone must make his grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling over' reverses GI D.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves are excavated, so making one is a matter of excavation with a spade.

clue.text: Considers what may lead to my signature

definitions.text: what may lead to my signature
definitions.meaning: a sign-off such as kind wishes coming just before the name at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone considers how to close a letter before signing.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider is to look upon; as a noun, kind wishes written before one's name close a letter.

clue.text: Old philosopher turns to very left-wing papers

indicators.note: turns means the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: red means communist, very left-wing
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: An old philosopher turns to extreme left-wing newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses TO RED ID. 'papers' means identity documents, not newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis, the 18th-century French Enlightenment thinker who edited the Encyclopédie.
